(module scope)

wasm-bindgen free() — drops the boxed struct AND unregisters the FinalizationRegistry entry, so the object never re-enters __wbg_*_free at GC time (the registry path is where a stale glue/wasm pair traps memory access out of bounds — the glue's free shim walks the struct layout compiled into ITS wasm, and a hot-swapped artifact pair makes that read land off the heap). Destroy calls it so the free happens deterministically while the artifact pair that built the object is still the live one.

(module scope)

Worker-routed probes — renders an end-state frame and reports the painted-pixel coverage ratio of the live canvas. Present only on worker-backed handles (main-thread mounts keep the readback in the caller); returns null on failure.

hasWebGpu

Capability gate — navigator.gpu is the WebGPU entry point. Separate from mount so callers can decide without touching the DOM.

webgpuWidgetsEnabled

webgpuWidgetsEnabled — the layer kill-switch. The WebGPU widget mounts (worker OffscreenCanvas route OR in-page) only run under ?debug=webgpuWidgets:active; every other state keeps the proven WebGL/CSS renderers authoritative. Re-parsed per call so tests and debug toggles flip without a reload.

  • @returns True when the WebGPU widget layer may mount.

sharedDevice

The page's single GPUDevice. Every widget artifact takes the SAME device object — WebGPU is designed for one device serving many canvases — because per-widget devices exhaust the driver: on Windows/D3D12 a busy page hit create command queue failed with E_OUTOFMEMORY after ~100 device creations, every subsequent requestDevice resolved a broken/undefined handle, and widget init trapped in the wasm future. One shared request keeps a full page of widgets inside any driver's device budget.

sharedFor

The navigator.gpu object the cached request was issued against — a different handle (test double, re-exposed API) re-requests.

getSharedGpuDevice

getSharedGpuDevice — request the adapter+device once and cache the promise so concurrent mounts share one acquisition. Keyed on the navigator.gpu object itself: swapping the handle re-requests. Resolves null on any failure (no adapter, rejected device request, undefined device) — every caller falls back to its WebGL/CSS path. A device that later goes lost clears the cache so the next mount re-requests cleanly.

  • @returns The shared GPUDevice, or null when WebGPU is unusable.

Mount options — drive selects the clock owner; see GPU_WIDGET_DRIVE for the semantics of each mode.

(module scope)

GPU_WIDGET_DRIVE member; defaults to RAF.

(module scope)

Default module loader — dynamic-imports the wasm-pack glue at /wasm/<slug>/<pkg>.js (see GPU_WIDGET_ARTIFACTS). @vite-ignore keeps vite from resolving build-optional artifacts; a 404 rejects and the caller falls back. Injectable for tests.

  • @param url Artifact glue URL.

moduleInitOnce

wasm-pack init is NOT reentrant-safe — __wbg_init checks the module-level wasm binding, then awaits instantiate: a second concurrent call before that lands re-instantiates and REPLACES the heap — widgets built through the older instance then run methods on the newer one's memory (RefCell flags read as garbage → try_borrow_mut fails → 'gpu slot poisoned', or state reads as zeros → a valid draw that paints nothing). Memoize the promise per module object so concurrent mounts share ONE instantiation.

initModule

initModule — the concurrency-safe wrapper around wasm-pack's mod.default(): the first caller's promise is the single instantiation; later callers join it.

  • @param mod The loaded artifact glue module.
  • @returns The shared instantiation promise.

warmWidgetArtifacts

Fire-and-forget fetch+compile for every eager artifact in the registry — currently just the skeleton, the loading placeholder itself. Calling this at the first skeleton mount starts the artifact fetch before init would, so the widget is ready the moment its canvas needs it; failures are swallowed because mount re-attempts and falls back anyway.

  • @param loadModule Injectable module loader (tests substitute a stub).

(module scope)

  • @param kind GPU_WIDGET_KINDS discriminant.
  • @param canvas The widget's dedicated canvas element.
  • @param loadModule Injectable module loader (tests substitute a stub).
  • @param options Mount options — GPU_WIDGET_DRIVE.MANUAL leaves the

initQueue

Widget-init serialization chain — each mount awaits the previous init's release, so the load-time mount burst pipelines instead of stacking inside one task.

taskYield

One macrotask boundary — setTimeout(0) via Promise; yields to input/rAF between consecutive widget inits. Kept as a named helper so the queue line stays a single expression and tests can stub the boundary if needed.

  • @returns A promise resolving on the next task.

withTimeout

withTimeout — bounds a promise: resolves its value when it lands in time, rejects otherwise. Used on the two unbounded GPU awaits — adapter/device requests and widget init — where a wedged driver or a dead device leaves the promise pending forever, which would latch the caller's mount-in-flight flag and starve its WebGL/CSS fallback.

  • @param p The promise to bound.
  • @param ms Deadline in milliseconds.
  • @returns The bounded promise.

wire

Attaches the rAF clock + resize/visibility plumbing to a live wasm widget. Separate from mount so the loop stays unit-testable without a real GPU. dt is seconds; the loop self-stops on destroy and skips frames while the tab is hidden (frame-budget rule). In manual mode none of that attaches — the caller's own loop calls widget.frame, widget.set_size, and widget.resize, so there is exactly one clock and one resize observer per widget.

  • @param widget Live wasm widget instance.
  • @param canvas The widget's canvas element.
  • @param manual True to skip the rAF clock + listeners entirely.

freeWidget

freeWidget — the deterministic counterpart of the FinalizationRegistry: calls the wasm-bindgen free() so the boxed struct is dropped now, under the artifact pair that created it, instead of at an arbitrary GC point (possibly after vite hot-swapped the glue — the __wbg_*_free shim then walks a stale layout and traps memory access out of bounds as an unhandled rejection from inside the registry callback, which no caller can catch). A corrupt free is contained here — the widget is already dead either way.

  • @param widget The live (or init-failed) wasm widget to release.

(module scope)

The worker's artifact spec — the registry entry's wire shape.

url

Glue module URL — /wasm/<slug>/<pkg>.js.

cls

Exported widget class name inside that module.

WORKER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS

Capability handshake timeout — a dead worker script never acks.

GPU_DEVICE_TIMEOUT_MS

Bound on requestAdapter/requestDevice — a wedged GPU process leaves these pending forever; normal adapters answer in tens of ms, so two seconds only trips on a genuinely broken stack.

WIDGET_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS

Bound on a widget's init(canvas, device) — pipeline compile on a healthy device finishes in well under a second; a dead/broken device traps the wasm future permanently (the E_OUTOFMEMORY case).

renderWorker

The live render worker — set once the probe acks.

workerProbe

One-shot capability probe latch.

pendingProbeAck

Probe ack resolver while the handshake is in flight.

pendingMounts

Mount ack resolvers — widget id → resolve(success).

pendingCalls

Async call/probe reply resolvers — replyId → resolve(result).

deadWatchers

Widget death watchers — id → callback when the worker reports dead.

workerWidgetSeq

Monotonic widget id — correlates worker records to proxies.

workerCallSeq

Monotonic reply id for call/probe round trips.

dispatchWorkerMessage

dispatchWorkerMessage — the single onmessage router for the render worker: mount acks, call/probe replies, and death notices.

  • @param e The worker message event.

(module scope)

spawnRenderWorker — create the worker and handshake it. The probe decides once whether this browser can render widgets in a worker — module workers + OffscreenCanvas + worker navigator.gpu; anything less routes every mount in-page permanently.

  • @returns True when the worker answered the probe as capable.

getRenderWorker

getRenderWorker — the capability gate for the worker route: resolves the live worker, or null when the browser can't run it.

  • @returns The render worker or null.

destroyRenderWorker

destroyRenderWorker — tears the render worker down for page unload and vite HMR dispose: terminates the thread, flushes every pending mount/call resolver (the map wrappers clear their own timers), fires death watchers so proxies report dead, and latches the capability off so nothing respawns inside a dying realm. Without this hook an HMR module re-eval orphans the worker — its per-widget pump timers keep the thread (and its browser process slot) alive forever.

(module scope)

mountViaWorker — attempt the off-main-thread mount: transfer the canvas to the render worker, wait for the artifact to init there, and wire a message-forwarding handle. Returns:

  • {handle} on success;
  • {canvas} when the transfer happened but the worker mount failed — the element is dead (placeholder mode, no context can ever attach), so it is marked in place and the caller's own fallback path takes over;
  • null when the worker can't run at all (probe failed or the canvas was already transferred).
  • @param spec The artifact registry entry.
  • @param canvas The widget's canvas element.
  • @param manual Drive mode — manual widgets pace frame messages from
